n: Ezekiel again sees the sapphire throne above the platform over the cherubim—the same chariot-throne from chapter 1, now at the temple.

f.w: sapphire stone
cherubims
f.g: Plural of cherub (the KJV adds an extra English -s to the Hebrew plural -im).

n: The man in linen is told to take burning coals from between the wheels and scatter them over Jerusalem. Coals that purified Isaiah’s lips now bring judgment on the city.

f.w: coals of fire

n: The cherubim stand on the south side of the temple, and a cloud fills the inner court.

f.w: on the right side of the house
f.g: The south side, as one faces east.

f.w: the cloud filled the inner court

n: God’s glory rises from the cherub and pauses at the threshold; the temple fills with cloud and brightness. At Solomon’s dedication the glory filled the temple; now it is preparing to leave.

f.w: the house was filled with the cloud

n: The cherubim’s wings sound like God’s own voice, heard all the way to the outer court.

f.w: the voice of the Almighty God

n: The man in linen goes in and stands beside a wheel to take the fire.

f.w: from between the wheels
f.g: From the heart of the fiery throne-chariot.

n: A cherub reaches into the fire and places coals in the man’s hands, and he goes out to scatter them. The burning of Jerusalem in 586 BC fulfilled this vision.

f.w: put it into the hands of him that was clothed with linen

n: Ezekiel notes again that the cherubim have human-like hands under their wings.

f.w: the form of a man's hand

n: He sees the four wheels beside the four cherubim, gleaming like a precious stone.

f.w: beryl

n: All four wheels look alike, each like a wheel set within another.

f.w: a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel

n: They move in any direction without turning, following wherever the lead faces.

f.w: whither the head looked
f.g: Whichever way the front faced, or wherever the leading cherub went.

n: Here even the cherubim’s bodies, backs, hands, and wings—not just the wheels—are covered with eyes, symbolizing perfect awareness.

f.w: full of eyes

n: Ezekiel hears the wheels called “the whirling wheels”—a name suggesting swift, storm-like motion.

f.w: O wheel
f.g: Hebrew galgal—“whirl” or “whirlwind,” a different word from the ordinary wheel.

n: Each cherub has four faces. Here the ox face of chapter 1 is called “the face of a cherub,” perhaps because a winged bull was a familiar cherub image.

f.w: the face of a cherub

n: The cherubim rise. Ezekiel now realizes these are the same living creatures he saw by the Chebar.

f.w: This is the living creature that I saw by the river of Chebar

n: The wheels move with the cherubim and stay right beside them as they rise.

f.w: the wheels went by them

n: When they stand or rise, the wheels do too, because the same spirit moves them.

f.w: the spirit of the living creature was in them

n: A sobering moment: God’s glory leaves the temple’s doorway and mounts the cherubim chariot. The Lord is withdrawing from the house his people defiled.

f.w: the glory of the LORD departed
f.g: This recalls the name Ichabod, “the glory is departed.”

n: The cherubim rise and pause at the temple’s east gate, with God’s glory above them. Each stage is slow, as if God is reluctant to leave.

f.w: the east gate of the LORD's house
f.g: The main entrance; the glory later returns by this same gate.

n: Ezekiel confirms: these are the creatures he saw beneath the God of Israel by the Chebar—now he knows they are cherubim, guardians of God’s holy presence.

f.w: I knew that they were the cherubims

n: Each has four faces, four wings, and human-like hands under the wings.

f.w: four wings

n: Their faces are the very same as by the Chebar, and each moves straight forward. The same God who appeared to the exiles is leaving Jerusalem—his presence is now with the faithful in exile.

f.w: they went every one straight forward
